summary: Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar around 1957–1959 and held a post at the British Library from circa 1973 to 1979.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Thomé H. Fang, Bingnan Li, and Lobsang Palden Tenpe Dronme. He taught at Chinese Culture University (1975–1980) and founded the Hwa Dzan Buddhist Library.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Harvard (~2003–2009) and studied at UT Austin. He held appointments at National Chengchi University (~2011, 2015–2020) and National Taiwan University (2021).

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and completed a PhD at Cornell University by 2008, supervised by Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti (1900–1972) was an Indology scholar. He served as a professor at Presidency University, held a post at Bethune College (attested 1941), and was Publication Secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).

Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar (1910–2007) worked in Indology. He served as Assistant Secretary at Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1941) and held a professorship at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University and served as its Director in 1996.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held leadership roles at Saijō-ji (~1947–1957) and Soji-ji (~1957–1967), and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968), served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (~1974–1986), and became a professor at Tokoha University around 1986.

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1905–1909) and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa, served as a professor at Otani University (1919), and co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society (1921).

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, University of Tokyo, and earned a doctorate at the University of Vienna (1990–1994), later serving as professor at the University of Tsukuba.

Chlodwig H. Werba (born 1947) specializes in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer, earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1982, and served as professor there (attested 1990–2006, 2022).
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Geshe Tsechok and the 13th Dalai Lama, and was appointed the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.
Chogyū Takayama (1871–1902) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School (~1886–1891) and the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896).
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (1829–1870) was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and trained under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).

Chris Clark is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon. In 2019, he held posts at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Sydney.

Chris Williams works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2026, he pursues postgraduate research at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Rita Langer while serving on the teaching staff.

Christiaan Hooykaas (1902–1979) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University (1921–1929) under Jean Philippe Vogel. He held positions at the University of Indonesia (1946) and SOAS University of London (1951–1953).
